bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in md_parse OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=511825301 ``` Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: md_parse md_html fuzz-mdhtml.c ```
bug_description.normalized: When admonitions are enabled, `md_process_line()` can treat a `[!tag]` line as an admonition continuation after the active quote container has already been dropped. The code still indexes `ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1]` without checking that a quote container is present, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read before the allocated container array.

source.description: First project parsing step that consumes witness markdown and materializes quote-container state from a `>` line.
source.value_from: The staged 840-byte witness is interpreted by `test/fuzzers/fuzz-mdhtml.c`: bytes 0-3 are `parser_flags = 0x2d5b935d`, which includes `MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS` (`0x80000`); bytes 4-7 are `renderer_flags = 0x5d205b20`; bytes 8-839 are passed to md4c as the 832-byte markdown payload. That payload contains quote-prefixed lines beginning with `>` (for example line 1 starts `>~~~...`) and later admonition-looking lines including the exact line `[!tIp-]`.
source.note: The later container array reported by ASan is allocated only after the witness first creates a quote container from one of these `>` lines.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The code reads the last container entry even though no active quote container remains.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports a READ of size 1 at `src/md4c.c:6543:21` on address `0x513000000028`, 24 bytes before the 384-byte `ctx->containers` region allocated from `md_push_container()`.

root_cause.description: The admonition-special-case gate checks only the parser flag and block-byte state. It omits the required guard that an active quote container still exists before later indexing `ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1]`.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `ctx->n_containers > 0 && ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].ch == '>'` here and removes the later assertion.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness splits the exact witness into parser flags, renderer flags, and the markdown payload later parsed by md4c.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Bytes 0-3 are `5d 93 5b 2d`, so little-endian `parser_flags == 0x2d5b935d`; bytes 4-7 are `20 5b 20 5d`, so `renderer_flags == 0x5d205b20`; bytes 8-839 are passed unchanged to `md_html(data, size, ...)` as the markdown buffer.

parser_admitted.code:
if(block->type == MD_BLOCK_QUOTE  &&  line->end - line->beg > 3  &&  line->end - line->beg < 16  &&
   CH(line->beg) == _T('[')  &&  CH(line->beg+1) == _T('!')  &&  CH(line->end-1) == _T(']'))
parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admission gate for the vulnerable path: the current line must be treated as an admonition lead line attached to a previously emitted quote block. On the staged witness, the exact line `[!tIp-]` satisfies this syntactic gate.

fine_trace.note: The exact witness sets `parser_flags = 0x2d5b935d`, which includes `MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS`, and passes the remaining 832 bytes as markdown to md4c.
Source. While analyzing an earlier witness line that begins with `>`, md4c consumes the attacker-controlled byte and materializes a quote-container descriptor.
The parsed quote container from step 2 is stored into `ctx->containers`. ASan's allocation stack points to this `realloc()` as the allocation of the array later read out of bounds.

When md4c later analyzes the admonition-looking line, that line does not present the active parent quote mark required by this loop, so `n_parents` stays below the existing quote-container depth instead of reusing the earlier `>` container.

Because no new child container was created for the current line and `n_parents + n_brothers` is 0 on this path, md4c leaves the previously active quote container. The callee loop at `md_leave_child_containers()` decrements `ctx->n_containers`, so the live container count reaches 0 before the admonition special case runs.

Root cause. This gate admits the admonition-special-case path based on parser flags and block-byte state alone. It does not verify that `ctx->n_containers > 0` and that the last live container is still `>` before the later index operation.

The function reloads the most recent emitted block record from `ctx->block_bytes`, sees `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE`, and treats the current witness line `[!tIp-]` as an admonition candidate. `md_ascii_case_eq(..., "tip", 3)` succeeds on the first three bytes after `[!`, so execution enters the inner body even though no live quote container remains.
Sink. With `ctx->n_containers == 0`, the expression reads `ctx->containers[-1].ch`, producing the left-of-buffer heap read reported by ASan before the subsequent `is_admonition` write can occur.

format.name: binary/fuzzer-flags-plus-markdown
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 840-byte witness at `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2026-718/poc` with sha256 `0f204742a2feaf1696e048e148d7730d7f750fcb61217938c0db9614fe722799`. Bytes 0-3 are little-endian `0x2d5b935d`, so the harness enables `MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS`; bytes 4-7 are renderer flags `0x5d205b20`; bytes 8-839 are passed unchanged as markdown. In that markdown, at least one earlier line begins with `>` and causes `md_is_container_mark()` and `md_push_container()` to create the `ctx->containers` array, and a later exact line is `[!tIp-]`, which satisfies the admonition lead-line syntax gate and matches the `tip` tag case-insensitively for the first three bytes. On this exact witness, md4c has already left the live quote container before processing `[!tIp-]`, but `ctx->block_bytes` still presents the last emitted block as `MD_BLOCK_QUOTE`; because the vulnerable gate in `md_process_line()` does not require `ctx->n_containers > 0` and a live `>` container, execution reaches `ctx->containers[ctx->n_containers-1].ch` and reads 24 bytes before the allocated container array. This contract is limited to that exact witnessed byte stream and state sequence; it does not claim that neighboring flag values, other `[!...]` lines, or other malformed markdown inputs follow the same path.
